worked.title: Q1 · Find β from momentum iterates; Cholesky; optimal GD step with an unknown β (10 marks)

problem.text: (A) f(x, y) = 3x² + 2y², GD with momentum β, α = 0.5, start (2, 4), (x₃, y₃) = (−7.36, 1.12). Find β. [4M]  (B) A = [[4, 2, 6], [2, 17, 7], [6, 7, 35]]. (i) Lower-triangular L with A = LLᵀ. (ii) All eigenvalues of L. [3M]  (C) f(x, y) = x² + βy², β > 0, start (1, 1). (i) Closed form for the optimal first step α. (ii) If α = 0.5, find β. [3M]

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: (A) reverse momentum [4M]. (B) Cholesky by hand and eigenvalues of a triangular matrix [3M]. (C) exact line search on a quadratic [3M].

steps.label: Notation
steps.text: This paper's symbols are kept: α = step size (η on the boards), β = momentum in (A) but an **unknown constant of f** in (C).

steps.label: (A) STEP 1 · Answer
steps.text: Unroll three momentum steps in each coordinate and match x₃ and y₃: the only value that fits both is **β = 0.4** (worked line by line in Lecture 11).

steps.label: (B) STEP 3 · Eigenvalues of L
steps.text: L is triangular ⇒ its eigenvalues are its diagonal entries: **2, 4, 5**.

steps.label: (C) STEP 4 · Optimal step formula
steps.text:
g = ∇f(1, 1) = (2, 2β), H = diag(2, 2β)
For a quadratic the exact step is α = gᵀg / gᵀHg
= (4 + 4β²)/(8 + 8β³) = **(1 + β²) / (2(1 + β³))**

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text:
• (B) Forgetting to subtract the earlier l² terms under each square root.
• (C) Using α = 1/(largest eigenvalue) instead of the exact-line-search formula.

steps.label: More
steps.text: (A) in full: [Lecture 11, Momentum tab](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/ch11/f-momentum/5).

worked.title: Q2 · Kernel trick on 1-D data; kernel matrix; hinge loss (10 marks)

problem.text: (A) Positive class {(7, 0), (9, 0)}, negative class {(8, 0), (10, 0)}. Using the kernel trick, find a suitable φ(x) and the decision boundary. [5M]  (B) X = [(4, −3), (0, 1)], φ(x) = [x₁, x₂, ‖x‖]ᵀ. Compute the kernel matrix K. [3M]  (C) Hinge loss of (y, y′) = (0.5, 1) and (1, −1); which sample is misclassified? [2M]

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: Choosing a feature map that separates the data [5M], K = φ(xᵢ)ᵀφ(xⱼ) [3M], hinge loss max(0, 1 − yy′) [2M].

steps.label: (A) STEP 1 · Feature and boundary
steps.text:
Odd x (7, 9) are positive, even x (8, 10) negative: no single threshold on x works.
**φ(x) = x mod 2** (1 for odd, 0 for even) separates them; boundary **φ = 0.5** in feature space (odd ⇒ +, even ⇒ −).

steps.label: (C) STEP 3 · Hinge loss
steps.text:
max(0, 1 − 0.5·1) = **0.5** (correct side, inside the margin)
max(0, 1 − 1·(−1)) = **2** (wrong sign ⇒ **misclassified**)

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: (A) φ(x) = x mod 2, boundary 0.5. (B) K = [[50, 2], [2, 2]]. (C) 0.5 and 2; the second is misclassified.

steps.label: More
steps.text: (A) [Lecture 16](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/ch16/worked/1) · (B) [Lecture 14, Kernels tab](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/ch14/f-kernels/5) · (C) [Lecture 15, Soft margin tab](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/ch15/f-soft/6).

worked.answer: (A) φ = x mod 2. (B) K = [[50, 2], [2, 2]]. (C) 0.5 and 2 (second misclassified).

worked.title: Q3 · Rows orthogonal to x (null space); sigmoid, log-loss gradient and Taylor (10 marks)

problem.text: (A) Ax = b, A is m × m with rows Rᵢᵀ, and every Rᵢ is orthogonal to x. (i) Find b. [1M] (ii) S = {x : Rᵢ ⊥ x for all i}: prove S is a subspace. [2M] (iii) If rank A = m, find S and its dimension. [1M]  (B) σ(z) = (1 + e^{−z})^{−1}. (i) Prove σ′ = σ(1 − σ). [1M] (ii) For f(x, y) = α ln(1/σ(x + βy)) + (1 − α) ln(1/(1 − σ(x + βy))), prove f = (1 − α)(x + βy) − ln σ(x + βy). [2M] (iii) Prove ∂f/∂x = σ(x + βy) − α and ∂f/∂y = β(σ(x + βy) − α). [2M] (iv) Degree-1 Taylor polynomial of f at (0, 0). [1M]

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: (A) null space as a subspace [4M]. (B) sigmoid algebra, chain rule and a first-order Taylor polynomial [6M].

steps.label: Notation
steps.text: This paper's symbols are kept: α, β are constants in f (not a step size or momentum). u = x + βy.

steps.label: (A)(i) STEP 1 · b
steps.text: Entry i of Ax = Rᵢᵀx = Rᵢ·x = 0 for every i ⇒ **b = 0**

steps.label: (A)(ii) STEP 2 · S is a subspace
steps.text:
S = {x : Ax = 0} (the null space)
Contains 0: A0 = 0 ✓
Closed under +: Ax = Ay = 0 ⇒ A(x + y) = 0 ✓
Closed under scaling: A(cx) = cAx = 0 ✓ ⇒ **subspace**

steps.label: (A)(iii) STEP 3 · Full rank
steps.text: rank A = m ⇒ Ax = 0 only for x = 0 ⇒ **S = {0}, dimension 0**

steps.label: (B)(ii) STEP 5 · Simplify f
steps.text:
1 − σ(u) = e^{−u}σ(u) ⇒ ln(1/(1 − σ)) = u − ln σ
f = −α ln σ + (1 − α)(u − ln σ) = (1 − α)u − ln σ ✓

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: (A) b = 0; S = null space; S = {0}, dim 0. (B) σ′ = σ(1 − σ); ∂f/∂x = σ − α, ∂f/∂y = β(σ − α); T₁ = ln 2 + (½ − α)(x + βy).

worked.answer: (A) b = 0, S = {0} when rank m. (B) T₁ = ln 2 + (½ − α)(x + βy).

worked.title: Q4 · PCA on four points from a figure (10 marks)

problem.text: The figure shows four points: (1, 0), (2, 3), (4, 1), (5, 4). Use cov(X) = (1/N)(X − μ)ᵀ(X − μ). (A) Principal components. [5M] (B) Components of the four points along PC1. [2M] (C) Percentage of variance captured by PC1. [1M] (D) If the points are rotated 90° anticlockwise, what are their components along their new PC1? [2M]

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: The full PCA recipe on 2-D data, and what a rotation does to it.

steps.label: Notation
steps.text: Points read from the figure: (1, 0), (2, 3), (4, 1), (5, 4). N = 4, 1/N covariance as the question says.

steps.label: (D) STEP 6 · After rotating by 90°
steps.text:
(x, y) ↦ (−y, x). The covariance becomes RCRᵀ = [[2.5, −1.5], [−1.5, 2.5]], PC1 = (−1, 1)/√2 (the old PC1 rotated).
A rotation keeps every length and angle, so the components are **unchanged: −2.83, 0, 0, 2.83** (up to the sign of the PC).

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: PC1 = (1, 1)/√2 (λ = 4), PC2 = (1, −1)/√2 (λ = 1); components −2.83, 0, 0, 2.83; 80%; unchanged after rotation.

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text:
• Using 1/(N − 1) when the question gives 1/N.
• Projecting uncentred points without saying so.
• (D) Recomputing everything instead of using "rotation preserves projections".

worked.answer: PC1 = (1, 1)/√2, PC2 = (1, −1)/√2; components −2.83, 0, 0, 2.83; 80%; same after rotating.
